title: Normal completion and completed regular birational model
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a commutative Noetherian normal local domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and put $C=\widehat A=\varprojlim_{r\geq1}A/\mathfrak m^r$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Suppose $f:T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is proper, $T$ is integral and regular, and $f$ induces an isomorphism of function fields [def-weil-proper-morphism] [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-pc-integral-scheme] [def-weil-regular-scheme] [def-sc-function-field]. Then $C$ is a complete Noetherian normal local domain, and $T_C=T\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}C$ is integral and regular [def-pc-fibre-product]. The base-changed morphism $f_C:T_C\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is proper and induces an isomorphism of function fields.

source.place: Tags 0BGI, resolve-lemma-regular-alteration-implies-local, part (3) in the birational normal case; 0BG6, resolve-lemma-port-regularity-to-completion, part (3). Integrality is the connected-normal argument in the proof of 0BGI; birationality is base change of the generic isomorphism.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $C$ is Noetherian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mC$ and residue field $A/\mathfrak m\ne0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] it is complete for $\mathfrak mC$. The map $A\to C$ is flat and surjective on spectra by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. Put $Y=T_C$. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change], $f_C$ is separated and finite type. It is universally closed: every base change of $f_C$ is, by the fibre-product universal property, a base change of $f$, hence closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus $f_C$ is proper. The spectra of $A$ and $C$ are locally Noetherian by the one-affine-cover definition [pqf-def-locnoeth], and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact]. Both $T$ and $Y$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\operatorname{Spec}C$ respectively. In particular $T$ is quasi-compact, and [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] makes it quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 0BG6, proof, proper base change and completion setup; Tags 0316, 05GI, 05GG and 00MC for completion properties.

proof.text: The morphism $f$ is locally of finite presentation by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth], since it is finite type and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is locally Noetherian. Both integral schemes $T$ and $\operatorname{Spec}A$ have just one irreducible component. The assumed isomorphism of function fields is the isomorphism on their generic local rings, and the generic point of $T$ maps to that of $\operatorname{Spec}A$. Separatedness therefore allows [lem-per-birational-isomorphism-dense-open]: there is a dense open $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $f^{-1}V\cong V$. In particular the generic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}(A)$.

source.place: Tag 0BAJ, lemma-birational-isomorphism-over-dense-open; used to verify the generic-fibre hypothesis of 0AY8.

proof.text: The scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is integral by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-domain-stalks-function-field], and its stalks are normal domains by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. The integral scheme $T$ is reduced and its sole generic point maps to the base generic point. Step 2 identifies the generic fibre and its global sections with $\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. All six hypotheses of [lem-trf-proper-normal-geometric-connectedness] now hold, so $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\cong f_*\mathcal O_T$ and hence $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)=A$. Flatness of $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ follows from the ring flatness of step 1 and [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-global-sections-qcqs] to obtain, as $C$-algebras, $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\cong\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)\otimes_A C\cong C$. The required quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness were checked in step 1.

source.place: Tag 0BGI, proof, third paragraph, global-section comparison; more-morphisms Tag 0AY8 and coherent Tag 02KH.

proof.text: Let $y\in Y$ lie over the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}C$, and put $x=p(y)\in T$. The canonical map $A\to C$ maps $\mathfrak m$ into $\mathfrak mC$ and induces the residue-field isomorphism of step 1, so $f(x)=\mathfrak m$. Apply [lem-per-closed-fibre-stalk-completion] with $X=T$. It identifies the maximal-ideal-adic completions of $\mathcal O_{T,x}$ and $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ by the homomorphism induced by the actual projection $p:Y\to T$. The base $A$ is Noetherian local as required; no regularity of $C$ or $Y$ has been used.

If $y$ is a closed point of $Y$, its image under the closed map $f_C$ is closed in the local spectrum $\operatorname{Spec}C$, hence is its unique closed point. Step 4 applies. The ring $\mathcal O_{T,x}$ is regular because $T$ is regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Both local rings are Noetherian: choose Noetherian affine neighbourhoods using local Noetherianity, identify their stalks with localizations by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], and apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Twice applying [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local], with the isomorphism of step 4 in between, shows $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ is regular. Every closed point of $Y$ has therefore been tested. By [lem-per-regular-closed-point-criterion], the locally Noetherian scheme $Y$ is regular.

source.place: Tag 0BG6, lemma-port-regularity-to-completion, proof of (2) and (3); properties Tag 02IT.

proof.text: By [rem-pc-regular-normal], the regular scheme $Y$ has normal domain stalks. It is Noetherian and hence quasi-compact, so [lem-sbc-normal-sections-finite-product], with $U=Y$, expresses $\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)\cong\prod_{i<n}B_i$ with every $B_i$ a normal domain. This ring is $C$ by step 3. As $C$ has the nonzero residue field $A/\mathfrak m$, $n\ne0$. As $C$ is local, $n$ cannot exceed one: for $n>1$ the product has an idempotent $e$ equal to $1$ in one factor and $0$ in the others, with both $e$ and $1-e$ nonunits. In a local ring both would belong to the maximal ideal, contradicting $e+(1-e)=1$. Thus $n=1$, and $C$ is a normal domain.

source.place: Tag 0BGI, proof, third paragraph; properties Tags 0569, 033N and 0358. Finite-product formulation uses the existing normal-sections node.

proof.text: The scheme $Y$ is nonempty, since its ring of global sections is the nonzero ring $C$. It is connected: a disconnection $Y=U\amalg W$ into nonempty disjoint opens would, by gluing the sections $0$ on $U$ and $1$ on $W$, give an idempotent $e\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=C$ with $e\ne0,1$. In a local ring an idempotent is $0$ or $1$: one of $e,1-e$ is a unit, and $e(1-e)=0$ then forces the other to vanish. This is a contradiction. The nonempty connected regular scheme $Y$ is integral by [lem-sc-regular-connected-integral].

source.place: Tag 0BGI, proof, third paragraph, connectedness and integrality of the completed model.

proof.text: Finally pull the isomorphism $f^{-1}V\cong V$ of step 2 back to $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Fibre-product universality [def-pc-fibre-product] gives $f_C^{-1}(V_C)\cong V_C$. The open $V_C$ is nonempty: choose any point of the nonempty $V$ and lift it by the spectrum-surjectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat]. Since $C$ and $Y$ are integral, these nonempty open subschemes contain their generic points and have the same generic local rings as their ambient schemes: restriction to an open neighbourhood does not change a stalk. To identify these local rings with the function fields, choose nonempty affine opens inside the isomorphic opens and apply [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] and [def-sc-function-field]. Consequently the isomorphism over $V_C$ identifies the function fields, through the map induced by $f_C$. Along with steps 1, 5, 6 and 7 this proves every assertion.

split_report.summary: Preserved the statement and the eight-step completion proof. Repaired absolute quasi-separatedness using the existing locally Noetherian scheme theorem, used the exact flat-ring-map/affine-morphism equivalence, and extracted the non-elementary 0BG5 completed-stalk comparison. Normality of C is derived by global sections and the finite-product theorem, integrality by the connected regular scheme theorem; neither conclusion is moved to a clause-restating helper.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q42-1fb40ca7a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: PASS, no fixes. I read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement, Stacks resolve.tex 0BG5, 0BG6 and 0BGI (third paragraph), and properties.tex 02IT and 02IL. The item is 0BG6(3) plus the 0BGI normal-case argument; hypotheses and conclusion are unchanged. Steps: 1 gives C Noetherian, local, complete and faithfully flat over A, f_C proper, and T and Y Noetherian, with T qcqs through the locally Noetherian theorem. 2 gets the dense open V from the birational node after checking all its hypotheses. 3 gets Gamma(T)=A from O_S = f_*O_T of the 0AY8 node, all six hypotheses checked, then Gamma(Y)=C by qcqs flat base change. 4 applies the new 0BG5 node at points of the closed fibre. 5: a closed point of Y lies in the closed fibre because f_C is closed; regularity crosses the completed-stalk isomorphism (both stalks Noetherian), and the new 02IT node gives that Y is regular. 6: the finite product of normal domains has exactly one factor because C is local and nonzero, so C is a normal domain. 7: Y is nonempty and connected by the idempotent argument, hence integral. 8: birationality by base change of f^{-1}V = V, with V_C nonempty. New nodes: the 0BG5 node is true (B/p^n = B'/q^n, then localize), the closed-fibre hypothesis is essential (Q(t) vs Q((t))), and it does not duplicate flat-local-completion-iso. The 02IT closed-point criterion is true by 02IL plus localization of regular local rings, and def-weil-regular-scheme states only 02IT (1)<=>(2). Neither node restates an item clause, and the snapshot and live DAG have no other node stating either. Batch 5: lem-trf-proper-normal-geometric-connectedness is the general Zariski connectedness lemma 0AY8, which neither assumption provides. Its own closure (1755 nodes) contains no trace-formula or Poincare-duality node except itself and a Mathlib leaf, and no nt-assume, sk-thm-trace-transport or batch-4 node, so I accept it; no non-trf 0AY8 node exists. The declared tool_uses are generic and accepted. No SGA citations.
